content:
According to NBC News, Apple's negotiations with OpenAI over alleged theft of trade secrets broke down because Apple's outside counsel accidentally sent an email to the wrong OpenAI employee, mixing up the communications between the two parties. Below are the details of the incident.

The report indicated that Apple's outside legal counsel mixed up two email recipients.

Last Friday, Apple filed a trade secret theft lawsuit against OpenAI Products and two former employees, Chang Liu and Tang Tan.

In the lawsuit, Apple accused its former employees of stealing confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's consumer devices business.

Apple also claimed that when the company first directly raised the issue with OpenAI in February this year, OpenAI did not respond:

However, according to NBC News, OpenAI said it had responded to Apple's initial outreach, but communications subsequently broke down because Apple's outside counsel sent an email to the wrong OpenAI employee, confusing that employee with another person.

The report indicated that Gabriel Gross of Apple's outside law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges sent an email to OpenAI's general counsel Che Chang, with the subject line "Former Apple employees retaining non-public, confidential, and proprietary information at OpenAI," accompanied by supporting documents for Apple's allegations.

Thirteen minutes later, Gross sent another email to Chang, thanking him for taking a call during that time and for "quickly expressing a willingness to cooperate."

The problem was that the second email was originally not meant for Chang, but for "a former Apple employee surnamed Wang who had jumped ship to OpenAI," NBC News noted. Gross had previously sent separate emails to Chang and Wang, and had also spoken with Wang by phone in between, but when replying, he mixed up the recipients and mistakenly sent it to Chang.

Chang believed Gross had sent him fabricated information to advance Apple's case against OpenAI, so he contacted two of Apple's in-house lawyers, accusing the company's outside counsel of "falsely claiming to have spoken with me on the phone," and added: "I don't know him, we have never spoken." He subsequently demanded that Gross be removed from the case.

Gross later apologised to Chang, and one of Apple's in-house lawyers told Chang that he could continue to liaise with Gross and his law firm during the proceedings. NBC News noted that "the negotiations appeared to end there," adding that OpenAI claimed "there is no record of any further contact from Apple's lawyers before Apple filed the lawsuit last Friday."
